Find (f⋅g)′(t), given that f(t)=20ti−2tj+(2+5t)kg(t)=t3i+tj+(t2+t)k

b

decision.explanation: The dot product is f(t)·g(t)=20t^4−2t^2+(2+5t)(t^2+t)=20t^4+5t^3+5t^2+2t. Differentiating gives 80t^3+15t^2+10t+2, which is option d.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\cdot g)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot {g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(20t)\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+5t)\,k \\  & =20\,i-2\,j+5\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+t)\,k \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j+(2t+1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdot g)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot {g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(20\,i-2\,j+5\,k)\cdot ({t}^{3}\,i+t\,j+({t}^{2}+t)\,k)+(20t\,i-2t\,j+(2+5t)\,k)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j+(2t+1)\,k) \\  & =(20{t}^{3}-2t+5({t}^{2}+t))+(60{t}^{3}-2t+(2+5t)(2t+1)) \\  & =80{t}^{3}+15{t}^{2}+10t+2\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\cdot g)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot {g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(20t)\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+5t)\,k \\  & =20\,i-2\,j+5\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+t)\,k \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j+(2t+1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdot g)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot {g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(20\,i-2\,j+5\,k)\cdot ({t}^{3}\,i+t\,j+({t}^{2}+t)\,k)+(20t\,i-2t\,j+(2+5t)\,k)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j+(2t+1)\,k) \\  & =(20{t}^{3}-2t+5({t}^{2}+t))+(60{t}^{3}-2t+(2+5t)(2t+1)) \\  & =80{t}^{3}+15{t}^{2}+10t+2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)=f′(u(t))u′(t)
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({e}^{u+1})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({e}^{2u})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\frac{1}{e}\,k \\  & ={e}^{u+1}\,i+2{e}^{2u}\,j+0\,k \\  & ={e}^{u+1}\,i+2{e}^{2t}\,j \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2})=4t\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & =f′(u(t))u′(t) \\ (f∘u)^{′}(t) & =({e}^{2{t}^{2}+1}\,i+2{e}^{4{t}^{2}}\,j)4t \\  & =4t{e}^{2{t}^{2}+1}\,i+8t{e}^{4{t}^{2}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Use the product rule: (uf)'=u'f+uf'. Here u'=2t and f'=[e^t,0,−e^(−t)], giving [(2t+t²)e^t,16t,(2t−t²)e^(−t)], which matches option b.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
{(u(t)f(t))}^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})=2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(u(t)f(t))}^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =2t[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 8 \\ {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+{t}^{2}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2t{e}^{t} \\ 16t \\ 2t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{t}^{2}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2t+{t}^{2}){e}^{t} \\ 16t \\ (2t-{t}^{2}){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Find (u(t)f(t))′ where f(t)=[et8e−t] and u(t)=t2.

a

b
[(2t+t2)et16t(2t−t2)e−t]

EXPLANATION

Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write (u(t)f(t))′=u′(t)f(t)+u(t)f′(t)

Let's find u′(t) and f′(t).

f′(t)=[ddt(et)ddt(8)ddt(e−t)]=[et0−e−t]u′(t)=ddt(t2)=2t

Therefore, we obtain:

(u(t)f(t))′=u′(t)f(t)+u(t)f′(t)=2t[et8e−t]+t2[et0−e−t]=[2tet16t2te−t]+[t2et0−t2e−t]=[(2t+t2)et16t(2t−t2)e−t]

content.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
{(u(t)f(t))}^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})=2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(u(t)f(t))}^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =2t[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 8 \\ {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+{t}^{2}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2t{e}^{t} \\ 16t \\ 2t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{t}^{2}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2t+{t}^{2}){e}^{t} \\ 16t \\ (2t-{t}^{2}){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Find (u(t)g(t))′ where g(t)=⟨2e−t,4ln⁡t,2⟩ and u(t)=12t2.

a
⟨te−t(2−t),2t(1+2ln⁡t),2t⟩
b
 ⟨t2e−t,t2(1+2ln⁡t),1⟩
c
 ⟨2−t,2(1+2ln⁡t),t⟩
d
 ⟨e−t,2ln⁡t,2t−1⟩
e
⟨te−t,1+2ln⁡t,2t⟩

decision.explanation: The product is u(t)g(t)=⟨t²e^(−t),2t²ln(t),t²⟩. Differentiating componentwise gives ⟨te^(−t)(2−t),2t(1+2ln(t)),2t⟩, matching option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
By the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
(u(t)g(t))^{′}=u(t){g}^{′}(t)+{u}^{′}(t)g(t).
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${g}^{′}(t).$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{e}^{-t},\,\frac{4}{t},\,0⟩ \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}) \\  & =t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)g(t))^{′} & =u(t){g}^{′}(t)+{u}^{′}(t)g(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}⟨-2{e}^{-t},\,\frac{4}{t},\,0⟩+t⟨2{e}^{-t},\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-{t}^{2}{e}^{-t},\,2t,\,0⟩+⟨2t{e}^{-t},\,4t\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2t⟩ \\  & =⟨2t{e}^{-t}-{t}^{2}{e}^{-t},\,2t+4t\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2t⟩ \\  & =⟨t{e}^{-t}(2-t),\,2t(1+2\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

By the scalar function multiple rule, we have (u(t)g(t))′=u(t)g′(t)+u′(t)g(t).

Therefore, we obtain (u(t)g(t))′=u(t)g′(t)+u′(t)g(t)=12t2⟨−2e−t,4t,0⟩+t⟨2e−t,4ln⁡t,2⟩=⟨−t2e−t,2t,0⟩+⟨2te−t,4tln⁡t,2t⟩=⟨2te−t−t2e−t,2t+4tln⁡t,2t⟩=⟨te−t(2−t),2t(1+2ln⁡t),2t⟩.

content.worked_solution:
By the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
(u(t)g(t))^{′}=u(t){g}^{′}(t)+{u}^{′}(t)g(t).
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${g}^{′}(t).$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{e}^{-t},\,\frac{4}{t},\,0⟩ \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}) \\  & =t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)g(t))^{′} & =u(t){g}^{′}(t)+{u}^{′}(t)g(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}⟨-2{e}^{-t},\,\frac{4}{t},\,0⟩+t⟨2{e}^{-t},\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-{t}^{2}{e}^{-t},\,2t,\,0⟩+⟨2t{e}^{-t},\,4t\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2t⟩ \\  & =⟨2t{e}^{-t}-{t}^{2}{e}^{-t},\,2t+4t\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2t⟩ \\  & =⟨t{e}^{-t}(2-t),\,2t(1+2\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the chain rule, we can write

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(u) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\,({u}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(6)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2u \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})={e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & =f′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2u(t) \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {u}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2({e}^{t}) \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {e}^{t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{2t} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
